finding.claim: GET /mirror passes the caller-supplied url query parameter to httpx without a valid host allowlist. The only check is a suffix match on the hostname, which also accepts attacker-registrable domains such as evilexample.com, and the resolved IP is never checked, so DNS rebinding can reach loopback, RFC 1918, or metadata addresses.
finding.source: mirror.py:11 (url: str query parameter on GET /mirror)

trace.note: url is read from the query string without normalization
only check: host.endswith("example.com"), no dot boundary
len(r.text) returned to caller as a size oracle

finding.guards_checked: Hostname suffix check (mirror.py:13) is bypassable by names like evilexample.com. Scheme is limited to http/https by httpx, not checked explicitly. No resolved-IP, private-range, or metadata-address check; no DNS pinning, so rebinding works. No port restriction. Redirects are not followed (httpx default follow_redirects=False), so redirect bypass does not apply. ALLOWED_SUFFIX (line 7) is defined with a leading dot but unused. Not executed: the bypass and DNS rebinding were not tested live, and a urlparse vs httpx parser differential (e.g. backslash in authority) is unverified.

verdict.guard_found: Only mirror.py:13, `host.endswith("example.com")`. This is a suffix match with no dot boundary, so it does not close the finding. Nothing else in the file validates the host, the resolved IP, the port, or the scheme. ALLOWED_SUFFIX at mirror.py:7 is unused. Redirects are not followed by default, which the candidate correctly notes.
verdict.reason: The url query parameter (mirror.py:11) is attacker-controlled on an unauthenticated route, and the only check at mirror.py:13 is a suffix match that accepts evilexample.com, so the unmodified url reaches httpx at mirror.py:16 with no closing guard. Every trace line matches the code: line 12 parses the hostname, line 15 creates a default client, and line 17 returns len(r.text) as a size oracle. The DNS-rebinding and parser-differential parts were not tested live, but the suffix bypass alone confirms the SSRF.
